_readme: Categories for the silent catches in server.js. docs/094.
This is a SIDECAR, not source annotation. Adding 79 comments to server.js would
be a large diff with no behaviour change to a file whose dependency mechanism is
construction order — churn with a risk attached. Keeping the categories as data
also enforces the rule the triage was written under: categorising a catch and
changing it are two different commits, and this file cannot change behaviour.
EXPECTED-OPTIONAL  the failure is a normal state and the fallback IS the design.
A price read that falls back to the cached value is not hiding
anything: the cache is the answer when the feed is quiet.
LOGGED             it should say something and currently does not. These are the
ones worth changing, and every one of them is a place where a
persisted state silently reverts to a default.
TODO-TRIAGE        not decided. The default. An unexamined catch has not been
Keyed by FINGERPRINT — the catch line plus its preceding non-empty line, hashed.
A catch that MOVES keeps its category; one that CHANGES loses it and is reported
as DRIFT. Line numbers rot: adding code above a catch used to hand it another catch's category, silently.
baseCommit: 91a318e (fingerprints; line numbers no longer used as identity)

priceReadWithCachedFallback.why: reads a live quote and keeps the previous value when the feed is quiet or refuses. The cached value IS the answer; the comments at 1648, 3267 and 4598 already say so.

optionalEngineStatus.why: reads a status field from an engine that may be off, unbuilt, or mid-restart. An engine that is not running has no status, and that is a fact rather than a failure.

derivedDataWithDocumentedFallback.why: a derivation whose fallback is stated beside it — previous day, default DTE, default step.

crashGuardOwnLog.why: server.js:70 writes the crash log from inside the crash handler. A failure here must not throw, or the process loses the original error to a second one about logging it.

notificationDelivery.why: telegram and alert delivery. A missed notification must never take down a monitor, and the inner catch at 2487 already logs the reason.

registryExpiryFailsClosed.why: safeExpiry: an unknown expiry leaves the risk layer's concentration check UNEVALUABLE and the order BLOCKS. The catch is the fail-closed path, not a swallow.

featureDetection.why: an optional require or capability probe. Absence is the answer being asked for.

fileMissingIsNormal.why: a per-day archive file that does not exist yet. ENOENT is the expected state on the first run of any day.

numericDerivation.why: an IV solve, a vol calculation or an OI sum that legitimately has no answer for some inputs. Each already yields null rather than a number.

bestEffortCacheWrite.why: a redis or market-state write whose only consumer re-derives the value anyway.

perEngineIndependence.why: emergency-stop disables each engine in its own try, so one missing engine cannot stop the others being stopped. That independence is the point.

persistedStateSilentlyReverts.why: THE GROUP THAT MATTERS. Each of these reads or writes a file that carries state across restarts — engine config, VRP history, paper positions, signal-health calibration. A failure here does not lose a tick; it reverts a setting the operator chose, silently, and the system then runs a configuration nobody selected. This is the same shape as the trade counter resetting on restart (docs/089 s1C).

backgroundWorkThatCanStop.why: consolidation, learner credit assignment and outcome logging. If these stop, nothing breaks visibly and the data they produce simply thins out — which is indistinguishable from a quiet market.

networkFetch.why: a call to yahoo, to the broker, or to this server's own port. A failure is worth a line: repeated failures are the signature of a token, a rate limit or a dead port, and none of those announces itself.

patternDetection.why: server.js:1325 catches around H/L pattern detection with `catch (err)` and discards err. The variable is bound and then dropped, which reads as an intention that was never finished.

absentVersusUnreadable.why: server.js:964 wraps the whole opt-candles archive read. The INNER catch at 961 already handles a bad file, so this one only fires on the directory itself — and it cannot tell 'no archive yet, first run of the day' from 'the directory exists and cannot be read'. The first is normal; the second silently reduces the caller to today's live bars, and thinner history looks exactly like a quieter market. One line naming the errno separates them.

_none.why: Empty. Every silent catch in server.js has been read and placed. This group must stay in the file: an empty TODO-TRIAGE is a statement that the work was done, whereas a missing one is silence.
